task_spec.title: High-cost claim identification
task_spec.objective: Medical management wants an early-warning model: when a claim comes in, how likely is it to end up among the most expensive 5 percent by paid amount, so a nurse reviewer can look at it early? Hold out a quarter of the claims to test on, define "high cost" as paid amount above the 95th percentile, and train a logistic regression plus one tree-based model. Report how well the models rank claims (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, and precision and recall among the top 5 percent of held-out claims by score). Produce the standard artifacts (model metrics, threshold, feature list, precision-at-k chart, report).

plan.rationale: Configured plan for high-cost claim identification. Use 25% test split per task requirement ('quarter of claims'). Define target as paid_amount > 95th percentile per task specification. Include comprehensive feature set covering claim characteristics (type, codes, place/provider, flags), service details (units, length of stay, admission type), and financial data (billed/allowed amounts), excluding identifiers and target-derived fields to prevent leakage. Train logistic regression plus random forest per task requirement ('logistic regression plus one tree-based model'). Apply standard scaling to optimize logistic regression performance. Include synthetic_data and class_imbalance caveats given 5% positive rate and experimental context; model_limitations caveat for responsible reporting. Enable show_denominators and cite_artifacts to improve transparency and reproducibility.
